audit.whatIsWrong: Nautilus's own page has phases[6].side/win[6] both saying 'Nautilus' for the 2+ items stage, but the already-audited mirror (audits/support/braum_sup__nautilus.json, on disk) explicitly flips that stage to Braum ('Late, Unbreakable blocks his Q hooks and your peel finally out-scales his single engage'). The two pages currently contradict each other on who wins the late stage.
audit.why: Braum's Unbreakable (E) blocks projectiles including Dredge Line (Q), and once he has tank items his peel/shield value out-scales a single-target engage in grouped fights — the same logic the mirror already used and that regression-check.js requires both sides to agree on.
audit.corrected: Flipped phases[6].side to Braum and win[6] to Braum in the same proposal, with matching why/whys text, to agree with the mirror.

audit.why: Spikes 0-2 (lvl2 instant-CC engage, lvl6 unstoppable R past his directional E, first-item durability) are concrete and kit-grounded; only the late spike/late content needed to agree with the mirror per point 2.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT) and named the owner's own W ('Titan's Wrath') instead of Braum's punishable timers; dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were verbatim tradeGood/tradeBad copies (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED); the knockup-enabler missingInteraction (both sides carry a displacement — Dredge Line vs Glacial Fissure) wasn't stated anywhere.
audit.why: Winter's Bite (Q) is 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s and stacks Concussive Blows toward the passive stun; Stand Behind Me (W) is a 12-8s leap that grounding/walls can deny; Glacial Fissure (R) is 130/115/100s and is a competing knockup against Nautilus's own Dredge Line.
audit.corrected: Rewrote breakdown.cooldowns with real numbers; dosFull[1].d now covers the knockup race (land Q before his Fissure); dontsFull[2].d now covers not standing in his fissure line post-R.

edits.before: Late Naut starts everything: R the carry through the formation and anchor whatever peels.
edits.after: Late, Unbreakable (E) blocks your Q hook and his peel value out-scales your engage in fights.

edits.before: You keep the edge at 2+ items: your engage dictates fights that Braum can only answer.
edits.after: Braum's Unbreakable (E) blocks your hook late; his peel out-scales your engage once itemized.

edits.before: Bait the answer, start the chain, and let your carry collect — engage trades are all-or-nothing; pick the all.
edits.after: Both sides carry a knockup — land Dredge Line before Glacial Fissure lands, or his chain wins the trade instead.

edits.before: Engaging into a banked disengage — the chain that starts answered is a donation with intentions.
edits.after: Standing in his fissure line after he R's stuns you before your own Q connects — reposition off the line.

edits.before: - Braum Unbreakable: matchup-defining — The shield wall eats your poke and engage projectiles — wait it out. The duo’s tempo bends around it. - Keep W Titan's Wrath banked for their best play. - The ultimate is a fight decision, not a habit.
edits.after: Winter's Bite (Q) is 8-6s and stacks Concussive Blows toward a 4-stack stun. Stand Behind Me (W) leaps on 12-8s but is dash-grounded. Glacial Fissure (R) is 130-100-80s; land your Q knockup before his fissure or his chain wins the race.

notes: The packet's own defect note (46.94% overall win rate vs a chart giving Nautilus all 7 stages) turned out to point at a real problem, but the fix came from the mirror rather than the raw win rate: braum_sup__nautilus.json (already audited) has phases[0-5]=Nautilus, phases[6]=Braum, and this proposal brings nautilus_sup's own page into agreement on that last stage rather than trusting the aggregate win-rate number directly. Levels 1-6 (phases[0-5]/win[0-5]) already agreed with the mirror and were left alone.
